specs.note: no elbows · stove top to termination

steps: Clearances

Parallel or corner, hold the lettered minimums A–J shown in the p. 8 drawing; the values are the same for residential and mobile home installs. Clearances may be reduced only by means the regulatory authority approves.
Floor protection

On a combustible floor, use a non-combustible floor shield (UL 1618-2009 Type 1; no thermal pad needed): USA 16" front and 8" either side of the loading door; Canada 18" on the door side, 8" other sides. Shield under the connector too, 2" either side.
Combustion air
In tight homes, balance intake air against HRVs, constantly running air handler fans, range hoods and dryers; a fresh air inlet into the stove's room is recommended. Consult an HVAC specialist.
Chimney

6" listed factory-built chimney to UL 103HT (USA) / CAN/ULC-S629 (Canada), or a code-approved masonry chimney with flue liner, serving this stove only. At least 3 ft above the roof penetration and 2 ft above anything within 10 ft.

Prefab: follow the chimney maker's instructions and buy every component (ceiling support package or wall pass through and "T" section, fire stops, insulation shield, roof flashing, cap) from that same maker. An interior run up through the ceiling and roof is recommended; an exterior chimney should get a chase.

Masonry (p. 11): have it inspected by a certified professional to NFPA minimum standards (no cracks, loose mortar, deterioration or blockage) and cleaned before installing. A stainless steel liner, preferably insulated, is recommended.

  • Never connect to a chimney serving another appliance (it voids the warranty) or to air distribution ductwork.
  • Maintain an effective vapor barrier where the chimney penetrates the exterior structure.
  • Comply with the local authority having jurisdiction and, in Canada, CSA B365-M87.
Chimney connector

6", 24 MSG steel (no aluminum or galvanized), kept as direct as possible, every joint fastened with sheet metal screws. Chimney support package through a ceiling; listed wall thimble through a combustible wall.

A chimney connector is required: don't install the chimney directly at the stove outlet. Flue pipe stays in the room, never through an attic or roof space, closet or similar concealed space, floor or ceiling.

  • Freestanding: double wall pipe from the stove top adaptor to the ceiling support box is recommended.
  • Wall exit: 3 ft of vertical from stove top to elbow is recommended; use a pair of 45 degree elbows rather than a single 90.
  • Canada: a minimum 18" (450 mm) clearance from single wall pipe.
Chimney height

Recommended minimum 15 ft from stove top to termination at 0 - 1000 ft, more at higher elevation or with elbows per the p. 12 table; no more than one offset. Add 2.0 ft per 90° elbow, 3.0 ft per "T" section and 2 ft per 1.0 ft of horizontal run.
Location & fan power

Insulated, habitable room, never a bedroom; in Canada, no alcove or fireplace. Fan kit: grounded three-prong plug into a grounded three-hole receptacle, cord not routed in front of or under the stove.

Freestanding space heater only. Don't cut or remove the plug's grounding prong.

Not designed for an uninsulated concrete basement or a shop/garage: the thermostat can stay calling for heat and over-fire the stove, and that damage voids the warranty (p. 16).

Note: the label (p. 4) says "not to be installed in any fireplace", while p. 13 bans alcove or fireplace installs in Canada only and, for the USA, says to adhere to minimum safe clearances.
Mobile home
Install the required kits first (outside air kit; fan kit or rear shield kit, where the manual differs). Double wall close-clearance pipe, roof exit only, tie-downs from leg anchor kit Z2872.

• Kits: outside air kit S.Z1726 / S.Z1726B plus a fan kit S.Z2814 or rear shield kit S.Z4015 (pp. 4, 13); install them before the stove.
  • Flue pipe: double wall, close clearance, CAN/ULC-S629 or ULCS610; single wall pipe is not allowed. Insulated chimney: listed factory-built, UL 103HT / CAN/ULC-S629.
  • Roof exit only. Follow the prefab chimney instructions precisely; ceiling support package from the same maker.
  • Fasten to the floor with the tie-downs in leg anchor kit Z2872 (p. 14). The chimney must be removed to transport the building.
  • Open area not used for sleeping; keep the floor, wall and ceiling/roof structure intact.
Note: on the kits required, the manual gives outside air kit plus fan kit or rear shield kit on p. 4 and p. 13, fan kit required for mobile homes on p. 14, and only "Outside Air Kit required" in the p. 8 table.
The manual prints the fan kit as S.Z1714 on p. 13; p. 6, p. 14 and the fan kit parts page (p. 38) give S.Z2814.
Outside air kit

Run the flexible metal hose through an exterior wall or up through the floor so it feeds up into the rear intake channel; it must never penetrate the wall above the channel's bottom. Keep it open at all times.
Installer notes & hand-off
Confirm every component is assembled, the bricks are positioned and the combustor and flame shield are in place. Fill in the installer notes on the back page and leave the manual with the homeowner.

• Don't operate without fully assembling all components; don't install damaged, incomplete or substitute parts (p. 5).
  • All bricks correctly positioned in the firebox (p. 20; brick layout p. 39).
  • Flame shield in place: triangle point down, resting on the two dome guard tabs and leaning slightly forward (p. 26).
  • Bypass: handle forward is open; rotated clockwise to the rear and pushed down to a positive click is closed (p. 18).
  • Record dealer, installer, phone, date installed and appliance serial number (p. 44).

items: Green or wet wood → check with a moisture meter

Poor draft or blocked chimney / cap screen → measure with a manometer, remove obstruction
Tightly sealed house → open a window slightly or install an outside air kit
Too much wood on too few coals → build a larger coal bed

Excessive chimney draft → measure with a manometer; install a cap
Wood too small → use larger pieces

Chimney too cold → use double wall stove pipe
Not enough vertical rise → minimum 36" before elbows; two 45s instead of a 90
Chimney not drafting → thermostat highest, bypass open, door closed, wait 5-10 minutes

light.title: Lighting a fire
light.html:
Build the fire on the bottom firebrick, never on a grate. Don't leave the stove unattended while the door is open.

  1. Check that all the bricks are in place. Set the thermostat to High and the fan (if fitted) off.
  2. Open the bypass (handle on the right pointing forward), then open the loading door.
  3. Put 10 balls of non-glossy paper toward the front and crisscross 20 pieces of kindling on top, leaving air gaps.
  4. Light it and leave the door cracked open.
  5. When the kindling is fully burning, add two or three medium logs. Keep the door unlatched until they catch.
  6. Latch the door. Leaving it open after the wood catches can make the combustor fail early. When the thermometer starts to climb, close the bypass.
  7. When nearly all the wood is burning and the needle is in the active zone, open the bypass and door, fill the stove with wood laid as far back as it goes, latch the door and close the bypass.
  8. Leave it on High until the fire is well established, then turn the thermostat down gradually.
Needle fell to inactive after turning it down? Turn the thermostat back up and let the fire re-establish itself.
Fan: the manual differs on when to switch it on; see Thermostat, bypass & fan.
First fires: the paint cures with a strong odor and some smoke. Burn on a low setting for several hours and open a door or window. A change in paint color is normal.

reload.title: Reloading the stove
reload.html:
Check the thermometer first. If the needle is still in the active zone, reload like this. If it has dropped to inactive, use the lighting steps instead.

  1. Have the next load ready. Turn the thermostat to High and wait a few minutes.
  2. Open the bypass and wait a few more minutes for the air flow to settle.
  3. Crack the loading door open and give it about a minute.
  4. Open the door slowly and load. If a lot of smoke spills out, close the door slightly until the chimney draws again.
  5. Latch the door and close the bypass right away. Leave it on High until the fire is well established, then turn it down.

On low you may see very little flame. That's fine while the needle stays in the active zone. A good time to reload: little wood left, a glowing coal bed, or the room cooling off.

Mild spring or fall days: the chimney draws less, so expect more smoke at the door. Run on High for 30 minutes after lighting or reloading, and burn smaller loads instead of turning the thermostat way down.

controls.title: Thermostat, bypass & fan
controls.html:
Thermostat knob

The knob is at the upper right rear corner. At High the stove burns fastest and gives the most heat; turn it counterclockwise for less.

  • Change the setting gradually. Too quick a change can make the thermostat work poorly.
  • The right setting depends on your house and chimney, so expect to adjust it.
  • The lowest burn rate is set at the factory. Altering it is against federal regulations.

Bypass handle

The handle on the right side opens a door that lets smoke skip the combustor while you light and load.

Pointing forwardbypass open
Turned clockwise to the rearclosed; push down until it clicks

A bypass left open causes too much heat and creosote, so close it when the steps say to.

Fan (optional kit)

About 30 minutes after the fire is established, match the fan to the thermostat: low with low, medium with medium, high with high.

Note: the lighting steps on p. 20 turn the fans on high as you close the bypass (step 7) and on after the initial warm-up (step 11); p. 16 says to keep them off until the stove reaches normal operating temperature.

thermometer.title: Reading the thermometer
thermometer.html:
The dial on top reads the exhaust after it passes through the catalytic combustor, the part that burns the smoke. It tells you whether the combustor is working.

Active zoneabove 500F, a clean burn
Inactive zonebelow 500F, not burning clean
  • Keep the stove in the active zone. If the needle drops after you turn it down, turn the thermostat back up.
  • Turn the fan off before you read it.
  • Turning the stove down early in a burn can make the needle climb for up to several hours. That's normal.
Note: the wait before turning the fan off is about 5 minutes on p. 18 and 10 minutes on p. 29 and p. 35.

Is the combustor working?

Compare the chimney smoke with the bypass closed and then open, waiting a few minutes each way. Closed should show much less. Look at the combustor at least three times each heating season. If the needle won't reach active, it may need cleaning or replacing; see your Blaze King dealer.

Note: p. 29 gives steps to clean and re-zero the thermometer, then says any thermometer maintenance must be done by a certified installer.

wood.title: What wood to burn
wood.html:
Burn natural cordwood only. Hardwood and softwood both burn well here; dense hardwood burns a little slower and longer.

Is it dry enough?

Aim for 20% moisture or lower: wood split, stacked so air reaches it, and kept out of rain and snow for at least 24 months. Wet wood wastes heat and builds creosote.

A moisture meter is the only accurate check. Split three random logs, take three readings on each split face (2" from each end and the middle, pins in line with the grain), and average them.

Never burn

  • Treated wood, coal, charcoal, colored paper, cardboard, solvents or garbage. Burning these materials may release toxic fumes and/or carbon monoxide, which may result in poisoning.
  • Flammable fluids such as gasoline, naphtha or engine gel
  • Wet, green or unseasoned wood. It can cause excessive creosote buildup. If that ignites, it can cause a chimney fire that may become a house fire and cause serious bodily harm.
  • Salt-water driftwood. It corrodes the stove and voids the warranty.
  • Chemicals or fluids such as gasoline-type lantern fuel, kerosene or charcoal lighter fluid, used to start or freshen up a fire. Doing so may lead to over-firing, resulting in a house fire and serious bodily harm.
Go easy on small, very dry pieces. Off-cuts, very dry small wood or pressed logs used in excess can overheat the firebox and damage it and the combustor.

glass.title: Cleaning the glass
glass.html:
The best way to keep the glass clean is to burn hot after every reload. Much of the film comes from moisture driven out of fresh wood.

  • Leave the thermostat on a higher setting for 30 minutes to an hour before turning it down for an overnight burn.
  • Long, very low burns leave deposits on the glass. Run on High for about 30 minutes to burn most of them off.

Cleaning by hand

  • Only when the stove and glass are cool. Never clean hot glass.
  • Use a soft cloth and no abrasive cleaners.
  • Rinse well with water afterwards. Cleaner left behind bakes on and is very hard to remove.
Protect the glass: don't strike it or slam the door, and don't run the stove if the glass or its gasket is broken. Replace it only with 5mm ceramic glass. Glass hit or cleaned with harsh or abrasive cleaners isn't covered by the warranty.

ash.title: Emptying the ashes
ash.html:
Take ashes out whenever they come within one inch of the door opening. Don't remove them all: wood burns best on a bed of ashes about 1/2" thick.

  1. Make sure the fire is out and the stove is cool to the touch.
  2. Put the ashes in a metal container with a tight-fitting lid. Don't put any other waste in it.
  3. Set the closed container on a noncombustible floor or on the ground outside, well away from anything that can burn.
  4. If you bury or spread the ashes, keep them in the closed container until every cinder has cooled.
Never store hot ashes in a garage or basement. They give off carbon monoxide and flammable gases.

The supplied poker has a hook for pulling the ash plug. The manual shows the rest of the ash drawer steps as pictures on p. 30. After the last fire of the season, remove all ash from the firebox and the ash drawer.

Vacuum only when the stove is cool. Hot ash can melt a vacuum bag and start a fire.

chimney.title: Creosote & chimney fires
chimney.html:
Slow fires make tar vapors that condense in the cooler chimney as creosote. The hotter the fire, the less creosote.

  • Inspect the flue pipe and chimney regularly through the heating season until you know how often they need cleaning, especially in the coldest months.
  • Have the chimney and the stove cleaned at least once a year, or as often as needed. A professional chimney sweep is recommended.
  • Open the bypass before sweeping so soot falls into the firebox.
  • In extremely cold weather, water vapor can freeze and block the chimney. Run on High for 5 to 10 minutes to melt it.

If a chimney fire starts

  1. Turn the thermostat fully counterclockwise and make sure the loading door and bypass are closed.
  2. Call the fire department.
  3. Check the chimney, attic and roof for anything hot enough to catch fire. Use a fire extinguisher or garden hose if needed.
  4. Don't use the stove again until you're certain the chimney isn't damaged. Have a certified chimney sweep inspect it.
Chimney fire damage isn't covered by the warranty. Make sure everyone at home knows the plan.

safety.title: Safety around the stove
safety.html:
• The stove is hot whenever it's in use. Keep children and pets from touching it.
  • Keep combustibles like clothing and furniture at least 48" from the front. Don't store wood inside the clearances or the space you need for loading and ash removal.
  • Run it with the door closed; open it only to add wood. Don't block the air openings or the space under the stove.
  • Have at least one smoke detector and one carbon monoxide monitor in the room with the stove, and more around the house. Never disable or move them.
  • If an alarm sounds, get everyone out. Fix the cause only once there's no risk.
  • Keep a fire extinguisher in a central spot everyone knows.
  • Never run the stove without the catalytic combustor, or with a missing or damaged door gasket or broken glass.
Surfaces stay hot long after the fire is out, glass included. Let the stove cool before any maintenance.

warranty.title: Warranty at a glance
warranty.html:
Blaze King's limited warranty covers the original purchaser from the date of purchase, for stoves bought from an authorized dealer and installed in the USA or Canada. It isn't transferable.

Catalytic combustor6 years: no charge years 1–3, then you pay 60% / 70% / 80% of retail in years 4 / 5 / 6
Stove body & steel firebox parts5 years: you pay 20% / 40% / 60% / 80% in years 2 / 3 / 4 / 5
Fans, modular thermostat, door handle steel parts2 years, parts and limited labor
All parts and materials, paint included1 year, parts and limited labor

Making a claim

Report the problem to your dealer within 30 days of noticing it, with proof and date of purchase. The dealer makes the claim in writing. A failed combustor goes back to the dealer with a combustor failure report and original proof of purchase.

Not covered

  • Gaskets, firebrick, and paint color change after firing
  • Over-firing (warped plates, burnt-off paint), misuse or neglect
  • Glass breakage that isn't thermal
  • Salt-saturated, driftwood or treated wood
  • Minor expansion and contraction noise. That's normal.
Summary only. Mail in the registration card; full terms are on pp. 40–43.

Cord wood only, built directly on the bottom brick with no grate. Load fuel only inside the usable loading area shaded in the figure on p. 19; loading any other space voids the warranty and is a safety hazard.

specOutput.title: Heat output & emissions
specOutput.html:
Under specific test conditions the stove delivered heat at rates from 10,094 to 36,076 Btu/hr.

Maker's website: Constant Heat Output (Low) 10,641 BTU's per hour for up to 30 hours; Constant Heat Output (High) 37,742 BTU's per hour for 10 hours.

Certified to the 2020 U.S. EPA particulate emission standards using crib wood (EPA test method 28R); tested and listed by OMNI-Test Laboratories.

Low burn0.20 g/hr · CO avg 0.03 g/min
Med-low burn (1)0.62 g/hr · CO avg 0.32 g/min
Med-low burn (2)0.46 g/hr · CO avg 0.39 g/min
Med-high burn1.23 g/hr · CO avg 0.81 g/min
High burn3.81 g/hr · CO avg 1.69 g/min
EPA weighted average0.81 g/hr

Efficiency is determined by the B415.1-10 method and stated as HHV (test fuel 19% - 25% moisture); the manual prints no efficiency percentage. The manufacturer-set minimum low burn rate must not be altered, and the stove must not be operated with the combustor deactivated or removed. The catalytic combustor supplied with the stove is Blaze King part # S.CAT203032.

Maker's website: HHV Tested Efficiency 83%.
The certification label prints "Combustor OEM part number: Z0336A-M" (p. 4); the combustor warranty section (p. 26) and the parts list (p. 37) give S.CAT203032.
Note: the Canadian standard is CAN/ULC-S627:2023 on the certification label (p. 4) and CAN/ULC-S628:2022 in the preface (p. 5); both pair it with UL 1482-11 (R2022).

specFlue.title: Flue pipe & chimney
specFlue.html:
Flue collar6" I.D. (152 mm)
Flue pipe6" diameter, 24 MSG steel; no aluminum or galvanized
Chimney6" listed factory-built for solid fuel, UL 103HT (USA) / CAN/ULC-S629 (Canada), or code-approved masonry with flue liner
Mobile home / close clearance6" listed double wall, close clearance connector with matching listed chimney

Don't connect to a chimney flue serving another appliance or to air distribution ductwork. Flue pipe is used only within the room. Listed factory-built chimney has either 1" or 2" insulation. Double wall pipe from the stove top adaptor to the ceiling support box is recommended for freestanding installs.

Canada: a minimum 18" (450 mm) clearance from single wall pipe is required.

specHeight.title: Minimum chimney height
specHeight.html:
Recommended minimum vertical height, stove top to termination, by elevation; columns are 0 / 2 x 15° / 2 x 30° / 2 x 45° elbows.

0 - 1000 ft15 / 16 / 18 / 19 ft
1000 - 2000 ft15.5 / 16.5 / 18.5 / 19.5 ft
2000 - 3000 ft16 / 17 / 19 / 20 ft
3000 - 4000 ft16.5 / 17.5 / 19.5 / 20.5 ft
4000 - 5000 ft17 / 18 / 20 / 21 ft
5000 - 6000 ft17.5 / 18.5 / 20.5 / 21.5 ft
6000 - 7000 ft18 / 19 / 21 / 22 ft
7000 - 8000 ft18.5 / 19.5 / 21.5 / 22.5 ft

No more than one offset (two elbows). Add for other parts: 90° elbow = 2.0 ft; "T" section = 3.0 ft; 1.0 ft of horizontal run = 2 ft of vertical rise. Sea-level example: 15.0 + 2.0 (one 90° elbow) + 4.0 (2.0' horizontal run) + 3.0 (one base "T") = 24.0 ft. The chimney must also be at least 3 ft above the highest point where it passes through the roof and 2 ft above any roof or obstruction within 10 ft horizontally (p. 10).

Note: the p. 12 table gives 19 ft for 2 x 45° at 0 - 1000 ft (4 ft over 15 ft), while the same page says two 45° elbows equal one 90° elbow and counts a 90° elbow as 2.0 ft.

These figures are guidelines; draft depends on the whole installation.

specClear.title: Clearances to combustibles
specClear.html:

B6" (153 mm)
C*25.5" (648 mm)

* In Canada, 18" clearance from single wall pipe is required. Clearances may only be reduced by means approved by the regulatory authority. Keep combustible objects at least 48" (1219 mm) from the front (p. 21).

specFloor.title: Floor protection
specFloor.html:
No thermal hearth pad is required. On a combustible floor, a non-combustible floor shield must be used; it needs no insulation value but must be listed under UL 1618-2009 (Type 1).

USA16" out from the front and 8" out from either side of the fuel-loading door
Canada (CSA B365)18" (450 mm) beyond any side with a door, for the full width plus 8" (200 mm) each side; 8" (200 mm) beyond other sides
Minimum size35" x 42.125" (889 mm x 1070 mm) USA; 45.5" x 52.125" (1156 mm x 1324 mm) Canada

Canada: less than 8" (200 mm) from a wall, the ember pad need only reach the base of the wall; don't place it on carpet unless it is structurally supported. A non-combustible shield is also required under the chimney connector, extending at least 2" either side. Blaze King does not recommend adhesive based vinyl flooring in front of the stove.

Required for mobile home (USA) and transportable building (Canada) installs; see the Mobile home step for the other kits.

conflicts.issue: Canadian test standard: certification label gives UL 1482-11(R2022) & CAN/ULC-S627:2023; preface gives CAN/ULC-S628:2022 & UL1482-11 (R2022).
Combustor part number: label gives 'Combustor OEM part number: Z0336A-M'; combustor warranty section and parts list give S.CAT203032.
conflicts.reason: Two numbering systems, not a misprint: the label gives the combustor's OEM part number (Z0336A-M); the warranty section and parts list give Blaze King's part number (S.CAT203032). The guide shows both.

conflicts.issue: Chimney height table adds 4 ft for a 2 x 45° offset at 0-1000 ft (19 ft vs 15 ft), but the same page states two 45° elbows equal one 90° elbow and a 90° elbow = 2.0 ft.

Fireplace installation: label says 'Not to be installed in any fireplace'; p. 13 prohibits alcove/fireplace installs in Canada only and for the USA says adhere to minimum safe clearances (p. 14 also mentions alcove installations).

Mobile home kit requirement: outside air kit plus fan kit OR rear shield kit (pp. 4, 13) vs fan kit 'required for mobile home or alcove installations' (p. 14); p. 8 table notes only 'Outside Air Kit required'.
Fan kit part number: S.Z1714 on p. 13 vs S.Z2814 on pp. 6 and 14 (Z2814 fan kit parts page, p. 38).
Fan-off time before reading the catalytic thermometer: approximately 5 minutes (p. 18) vs 10 minutes (pp. 29, 35).
Thermometer maintenance: p. 29 gives owner steps to clean the probe and re-zero the dial, then states any thermostat or thermometer maintenance must be completed by a certified installer.

Fan timing at light-off: step 7 says turn fan(s) on to high when closing the bypass; step 11 says turn the fan on after the initial warm-up; p. 16 says fans off until the stove reaches normal operating temperatures.
